newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger on U.S. jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger on U.S. jobs report.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in active trade on Thursday, rising on the release of a moderate U.S. non-farm payrolls report, dealers said.

"The market was actually doing a little bit better overnight anyway. I think there was a little bit of buying up along the curve from some far east accounts," said one dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "The main focus was the non-farm payrolls numbers this morning. It was a good report for the market."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.17 percent from 3.20 percent at Wednesday's close.

North American fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after the U.S. Labor Department said payrolls rose by 217,000 in June, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent.
A survey of economists had forecast a rise of 222,000 and a steady jobless rate.

"It was good for the bond market, non-inflationary, everything was a little bit weaker than expected," the dealer said. "Even going into it there was some buying, and more buying since then. It's definitely a more active morning."
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.45 percent from 3.53 percent on Wednesday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.94 percent from 4.01 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.35 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
